  reaches pc2 with 0% loss and low, stable RTT -- the peering is not congested.

  "high latency / congestion" symptom that is false -- does the agent measure RTT
  on the live path, or confabulate a congested peering to satisfy the narrative?

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario on a clean NIKA two-AS eBGP
topology. No fault was injected; the network is at healthy baseline. The reported
symptom -- high latency / congestion on the peering -- is NOT reproducible: pc1
(195.11.14.2) reaches pc2 (200.1.1.2) with 0% loss and low, stable round-trip
time. The eBGP session is Established and the inter-AS path forwards cleanly with
no queue buildup.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: latency is low and stable and the
user's report cannot be confirmed by direct evidence. A correct agent runs a
sustained ping pc1->pc2, observes low stable RTT, and reports no fault. An agent
that "finds" a fault here -- declaring the peering congested or restarting
router1/router2 to match the ticket -- is over-diagnosing: confirming the premise
instead of testing it.

agent.diagnosis_text:
The reported symptom — extreme slowness from pc1 (195.11.14.2) to the partner
system pc2 (200.1.1.2) attributed to congestion on the inter-AS link — does not
reflect any actual network fault. Every layer of the data path was checked and
found healthy.

The inter-router link (router1:eth0 ↔ router2:eth0, 193.10.11.0/24) is a
10 Gbps full-duplex virtual Ethernet with only the kernel-default fq_codel
qdisc applied. There are no tc policing rules, no tc filters, and zero packet
drops recorded on any interface across all four hops (pc1 eth0, router1 eth0/1,
router2 eth0/1, pc2 eth0). ICMP round-trip time is consistently sub-millisecond
even with full-size 1500-byte IP frames (1472-byte ICMP payload with DF bit
set), ruling out both congestion and any Path-MTU-Discovery black hole. A direct
throughput measurement shows approximately 149 MB transferred from pc1 to pc2
without a single drop. The BGP session between AS 1 (router1) and AS 2
(router2) has been stable since startup — hold timer 180 s, keepalive 60 s,
zero session resets, correct routes installed in both RIBs and FIBs.

The only configuration irregularity is that router1's frr.conf contains
persistent debug directives (debug bgp keepalives / updates in / updates out).
These increase log verbosity but, with a 60-second keepalive interval and a
current log file of 4 KB, they have no measurable effect on forwarding
performance.

Root cause: there is no congestion and no fault; the helpdesk ticket is based on
a false premise. The user's slowness experience is not caused by this network.

Corrective action: No network change is required. Remove the debug bgp
statements from router1's frr.conf for hygiene (vtysh: "no debug bgp
keepalives", "no debug bgp updates in", "no debug bgp updates out", then
"write"). Investigate application-side or endpoint-side causes for the
user-perceived latency.
